probe: 64 sequences of 100 bytes, each shown twice in one window: random lowercase letters, and random words (3 to 9 letters) of the enwik8 training split joined by spaces (experiments/copy_probe.py, seed 7). The first copy cannot be predicted beyond the statistics of letters and words; the second can be by finding the same bytes earlier and reading what followed them. Pairs are bits a byte on the first copy and on the second after its first 8 bytes. Uniformly random bytes were tried first and no model, the Transformer included, copied them: they lie outside the text the models learned.
reading: On the small test bed copying is rare and decides the best runs: of four seeds of the plain stack only the best (1.9578) copies, and the 12-level stack with twice the parameters copies most and scores best. At full size the stack copies better than the Transformers trained on the same windows (0.23 to 0.31 bits a byte on the second copy against 0.36 to 0.81), and is no worse on the first copy. Copying is not where the full-size stack loses to the Transformer; it loses on what real text asks beyond it.
